riddle: I am the largest animal on land. I use my long trunk to drink, lift logs and spray water over my back, and I flap my big ears to keep cool. What am I?
hint: Famous for never forgetting.

riddle: I am the tallest animal alive. My neck is extremely long, yet it has the same number of bones as yours. My coat is covered in brown patches. What am I?
hint: I nibble leaves from the tops of acacia trees.

riddle: I hop across Australia on two powerful back legs, balance with my thick tail, and I am the biggest of all the pouched animals. My baby rides in my pouch. What am I?
hint: My baby is called a joey.

riddle: I dance to tell my sisters where the flowers are, I live in a hive with one queen, and I make a sweet golden food. If I sting you, I die. What am I?
hint: Buzz.

riddle: I hunt at night, can turn my head much further round than you can, and soft feathers let me fly almost silently. People call me wise. What bird am I?
hint: Hoo hoo.

riddle: I am India's national bird. When I want to impress, I spread a huge fan of tail feathers covered in shiny eye-shaped spots. What am I?
hint: I dance when the monsoon clouds arrive.

riddle: I carry my house on my back, glide very slowly on one slimy foot, and leave a shiny trail behind me. What am I?
hint: Garden lettuce is my favourite.

riddle: I have eight legs and no wings, and I spin silk into a sticky web to trap flies. What am I?
hint: Not an insect, whatever people say.

riddle: I begin life as a hungry caterpillar, rest inside a chrysalis, and come out with bright wings to sip nectar from flowers by day. What am I?
hint: Colourful and fluttery.

riddle: I am tiny and whine near your ear at night. Only the females of my kind bite for blood, and some of us spread malaria and dengue. What am I?
hint: Keep the net closed.

riddle: I am called the ship of the desert. I can go days without a drink, and the hump on my back stores fat, not water. What am I?
hint: Rajasthan's favourite ride.

riddle: I am a bird that cannot fly but swims superbly. I live mostly in the southern half of the world, waddle when I walk, and dress in black and white like a waiter. What am I?
hint: Antarctica is full of us.

riddle: I walk slowly on land under a hard domed shell, and in a famous fable I beat a boastful hare in a race. What am I?
hint: Slow and steady wins the race.

riddle: I look like a horse wearing a black-and-white striped coat, and I roam the grasslands of Africa in herds. What am I?
hint: Some say I'm white with black stripes, others the reverse.

riddle: I am the largest cat in the world and India's national animal. My orange coat has black stripes, and unlike most cats I love a swim. What am I?
hint: Sundarbans is one of my homes.

riddle: I am a green bird with a curved red beak, and I can copy the words people say to me. What am I?
hint: People say I like green chillies.

riddle: I start life as a tadpole in a pond, grow legs and lose my tail, then leap about with smooth wet skin, catching insects with my sticky tongue and croaking. What am I?
hint: Monsoon night singer.

riddle: I am the only mammal that can truly fly. I sleep hanging upside down during the day and come out at dusk. What am I?
hint: Batman borrowed my name.

riddle: I am tiny, I live in a colony with a queen, and I can carry many times my own weight. Leave sugar on the table and I'll march in a line to find it. What am I?
hint: Hardworking, according to every teacher.

riddle: I am a beetle that flashes a light from my tail as I fly on warm nights, signalling to find a mate. What am I?
hint: A living torch.

riddle: I am a tall yellow flower whose young head turns to follow the sun across the sky. My seeds are a popular snack. What am I?
hint: My Hindi name means sun-face.

riddle: I am India's national flower. I grow up out of muddy ponds, yet my pink petals rise clean above the water. What am I?
hint: Mud below, beauty above.

riddle: I grow in dry deserts, store water in my thick green stem, and have sharp spines instead of leaves. What am I?
hint: Don't hug me.

riddle: I am called the king of fruits in India. Alphonso is one of my famous varieties, and my sweet yellow flesh surrounds one big flat seed. What am I?
hint: Summer's most awaited fruit.

riddle: I grow in bunches called hands, and you peel off my yellow skin before you eat me. What am I?
hint: Monkeys love me.

riddle: Chop me and I make you cry. I grow underground in layers, and I start almost every Indian curry. What am I?
hint: When my price rises, it makes the news.

riddle: I have a hairy brown shell, sweet water inside and white flesh, and I fall from a tall palm tree. What am I?
hint: Kerala has plenty of me.

riddle: I am green outside, red and juicy inside, with black seeds scattered through me. I'm a summer favourite. What am I?
hint: Big, heavy and mostly water.

riddle: I appear when sunlight shines through raindrops. I am an arc of colours running from red to violet. What am I?
hint: VIBGYOR.

riddle: I fall from winter clouds as a tiny six-sided ice crystal, and people say no two of me are exactly alike. What am I?
hint: Catch me on your tongue.

riddle: I am a giant spark of electricity that flashes out of a storm cloud. You see me first and hear the rumble I cause a moment later. What am I?
hint: Stay away from tall trees when I'm around.

riddle: I circle the Earth about once a month. I have no light of my own, yet I shine at night by reflecting the Sun. What am I?
hint: Full, half or crescent.

riddle: I am the star at the centre of our solar system. Every planet circles me, and my light takes about eight minutes to reach you. What am I?
hint: Don't look straight at me.

riddle: I am a muscle in your chest that never takes a holiday. I pump blood around your body, beating about 60 to 100 times a minute. What am I?
hint: Bollywood sings about me constantly.

riddle: I live in your mouth, help you taste sweet and salty, and push food around while you chew. What am I?
hint: Stick me out at the doctor.

riddle: I am water that got too cold. I float in your glass because I'm less dense than the liquid I came from. What am I?
hint: Your cold drink needs me.

riddle: I pull iron nails towards me without touching them. I have a north pole and a south pole, and my like poles push each other away. What am I?
hint: Fridges wear me as decoration.

riddle: I am made of countless tiny water droplets floating in the sky. When I turn dark and heavy, rain may fall. What am I?
hint: Sometimes I look like animals.

riddle: I am the third planet from the Sun and the only one known to have life. Most of my surface is covered with water. What am I?
hint: You're standing on me.

riddle: I am the fastest land animal, sprinting over 100 km per hour. My golden coat has solid black spots, and black tear lines run down my face. What am I?
hint: Recently brought back to Kuno in India.

riddle: I am a clever black-and-grey bird common in Indian cities. I call 'caw caw', and people say my calling means guests are coming. What am I?
hint: I steal food from balconies.

riddle: I am a snake that rises up and spreads a hood with a spectacle-like mark on the back when threatened. Snake charmers once made me sway by waving their pipes in front of me. What am I?
hint: Hisss, and a hood.

riddle: I live in the sea, have exactly eight arms lined with suckers, three hearts, and I squirt ink to escape. What am I?
hint: Paul, one of my kind, 'predicted' World Cup results.

riddle: I am the largest animal on Earth. I live in the ocean and breathe air through a blowhole, yet I feed on tiny shrimp-like krill. What am I?
hint: Big, blue and not a fish.

riddle: I am a flower famous for love and Valentine's Day. I smell sweet, but mind the sharp prickles on my stem. What am I?
hint: Red is my most famous colour.

riddle: I am small, green or red, and I set your mouth on fire. Indian food would be bland without me. What am I?
hint: Pickled, fried or raw, I bring the heat.

riddle: I grow underground, have little 'eyes' on my skin, and I can become chips, fries or a spicy samosa filling. What am I?
hint: I go with almost every sabzi.

riddle: There are two of us in your chest. We fill with air when you breathe in and pass oxygen into your blood. What are we?
hint: Smoking hurts us.

riddle: I let you see the world. I blink many times a minute, can be brown, blue or green, and I water up when you chop onions. What am I?
hint: Two of us sit on your face.

riddle: Feed me wood and I grow; pour water on me and I die. I need oxygen to live, and I give off heat and light. What am I?
hint: Bonfire nights are all about me.

riddle: I am a mountain that can erupt, spilling red-hot lava and ash from the crater at my top. What am I?
hint: Barren Island in the Andamans is one of me.

riddle: I have webbed feet and a flat orange bill, I paddle on ponds, and I say 'quack'. What am I?
hint: Donald is my most famous cousin.

riddle: I drum my beak hard against tree trunks to find insects and to dig out a hole for my nest. What bird am I?
hint: Tap tap tap on the bark.

riddle: I live on the seabed, usually have five arms, and if I lose one I can grow it back. Despite my name, I am not a fish. What am I?
hint: I'm shaped like something in the night sky.

riddle: An adult human has 206 of us. We hold you up, protect your organs, and one of us in your thigh is the longest you have. What are we?
hint: Drink milk for us, they say.

riddle: I am an orange root that grows underground, and in winter I become the star of a famous halwa. What am I?
hint: Rabbits in cartoons munch me.

riddle: I can move each eye in a different direction, catch insects with a tongue longer than my body, and change the colour of my skin. What am I?
hint: A person who changes sides is called one of me.

riddle: I am the only bird that can fly backwards. My wings beat so fast they make a buzzing sound, and I sip nectar while hovering in place. What am I?
hint: My name comes from the noise my wings make.

riddle: I am so slow that green algae grows in my fur. I hang upside down in Central and South American rainforests and climb down only about once a week to use the toilet. What am I?
hint: My name is also one of the seven deadly sins.

riddle: I live in Australia, sleep up to 20 hours a day, and eat almost nothing but eucalyptus leaves. People call me a bear, but I carry my baby in a pouch. What am I?
hint: Cuddly-looking tree-hugger.

riddle: I am a mammal that lays eggs. I have a bill like a duck, a tail like a beaver, and the males carry venomous spurs on their back legs. What am I?
hint: Scientists once thought I was a hoax.

riddle: I am a fish that swims upright, curls my tail around seaweed to hold on, and wears bony armour instead of scales. In my family it is the father who carries the eggs in a pouch and gives birth. What am I?
hint: Dads do the heavy lifting here.

riddle: I am small and pale, I build huge mud mounds, and I love eating wood, including your furniture. People often mistake me for an ant, but my closest relatives are actually cockroaches. What am I?
hint: Pest control's favourite enemy.

riddle: I am a caterpillar who feeds on mulberry leaves. The cocoon I spin is unwound into thread for a shiny, expensive fabric. What am I?
hint: Kanjeevaram sarees owe me a lot.

riddle: I am a plant that eats insects. When a fly brushes the tiny hairs on my leaves twice in quick succession, my leaves snap shut like jaws. What am I?
hint: Named after a goddess.

riddle: I wear a crown but I'm no king, and I have scales but I'm no fish. I'm sweet and yellow inside, and I'm really many small fruits fused into one. What am I?
hint: SpongeBob lives in one of me.

riddle: Botanists call me a fruit, but cooks treat me as a vegetable. I am red and juicy, and I'm the base of ketchup. What am I?
hint: Salad, chutney, sauce: I'm in all.

riddle: I grow as a bulb made of many cloves wrapped in papery skin. Legend says I scare off vampires, and I definitely scare off people close to your breath. What am I?
hint: Peel me for tadka.

riddle: I am a red, heart-shaped fruit dotted with tiny specks on the outside. Each speck is really a little fruit holding its own seed, and I'm famously served with cream. What am I?
hint: Mahabaleshwar grows lots of me.

riddle: Shout into a valley or an empty hall and I answer you with your own words, a moment late. I have no mouth and never speak first. What am I?
hint: Sound that comes back.

riddle: I follow you on sunny days. I'm longest in the early morning and evening, shortest around noon, and I vanish in the dark. What am I?
hint: Peter Pan lost his.

riddle: I am a cloud of tiny water droplets that sits right on the ground. On winter mornings I delay trains and flights because you can barely see through me. What am I?
hint: Delhi in January knows me well.

riddle: I appear as tiny drops on grass early in the morning even though it didn't rain. I form when the air cools overnight and can't hold its water. What am I?
hint: Wet feet on a morning lawn.

riddle: I am balls of ice that fall from thunderstorm clouds, sometimes big enough to dent cars, even in the middle of summer. What am I?
hint: Clattering on a tin roof.

riddle: I am a dirty snowball from the far edge of the solar system. When I swing close to the Sun I grow a glowing tail that always points away from it. What am I?
hint: Halley is my famous cousin.

riddle: Rusty iron dust turns my surface red, I have two tiny potato-shaped moons, and robot rovers from Earth crawl over me. What am I?
hint: ISRO sent an orbiter to me in 2013.

riddle: I'm a gas giant, the second-largest planet, yet so light for my size that I'd float in a big enough bathtub. My biggest moon, Titan, has lakes of liquid methane. What am I?
hint: Sixth from the Sun.

riddle: I'm not a star at all, just a speck of space rock burning up as it streaks through the air. Still, people make a wish when they see me. What am I?
hint: Look up during a meteor shower.

riddle: I am your body's largest organ. I keep germs out, sweat to cool you down, and I darken when I spend time in the sun. What am I?
hint: Sunscreen protects me.

riddle: Everyone has me, yet no two people share the same one, not even identical twins. Detectives dust for me on glasses and doorknobs. What am I?
hint: Your phone may unlock with me.

riddle: I weigh a bit more than a 1 kg bag of sugar, use about a fifth of your body's energy, and I'm working on this riddle right now. What am I?
hint: Grey matter.

riddle: When you're cold or scared, tiny muscles pull your hairs upright and I pop up as little bumps all over your arms. What am I?
hint: A great song can give you these.

riddle: I am a sudden jerk of the muscle under your lungs that makes you go 'hic'. People try holding their breath or sipping water to get rid of me. What am I?
hint: Some say someone is remembering you.

riddle: I am what water becomes when it gets hot enough. I rise from a boiling kettle, and I once pulled trains across India. What am I?
hint: Idlis are cooked in me.

riddle: I creep over old iron gates and bicycles during the monsoon, turning them orange-brown and flaky. A coat of paint keeps me away. What am I?
hint: Iron plus water plus air.

riddle: You can't see me, but I keep your feet on the floor, make apples fall, and hold the Moon in its orbit. What am I?
hint: Newton and an apple.

riddle: Once in a while the Moon slides exactly between the Sun and the Earth, and for a few minutes daytime turns dark. What is this event called?
hint: Watch it only through special glasses.

riddle: I am a large rodent covered in long sharp quills. I can't shoot them, but they come loose easily and stick in any animal that attacks me. What am I?
hint: Hugging me is a bad idea.

riddle: I am an Indian bird; the males are glossy black with red eyes. I lay my eggs in crows' nests so they raise my chicks, and my sweet call rings out in the hot months. What am I?
hint: Singers with sweet voices are compared to me.

riddle: I am a small yellow-and-brown bird who weaves strips of grass into a hanging, bottle-shaped nest, often dangling over water. What am I?
hint: An expert at knitting a home.

riddle: I am a pink bird that often stands on one leg. My colour comes from the shrimp and algae I eat, and I feed with my head upside down. What am I?
hint: Gujarat's Rann of Kutch hosts huge flocks of me.

riddle: I live in the sea but breathe air, find food with clicks and echoes, and have a beak-like snout. I love leaping beside boats, and I'm a mammal, not a fish. What am I?
hint: Flipper was one of me.

riddle: I am a fish with no bones at all, only cartilage. I keep growing new teeth my whole life, and my fin slicing the water scares swimmers. What am I?
hint: Jaws.

riddle: I have no shell of my own, so I borrow empty snail shells and move house whenever I outgrow one. What am I?
hint: A crab who keeps to himself.

riddle: I am not a plant: I have no leaves and no green at all. I pop up after rain, often shaped like a little umbrella, and some of me are tasty while others are deadly. What am I?
hint: Mario grows bigger by eating me.

riddle: I am an Indian tree whose bitter leaves keep insects away. People have long chewed my twigs to clean their teeth. What am I?
hint: Bitter, but good for you.

riddle: I am India's national tree. My branches drop roots that grow into new trunks, so one of me can look like a small forest. What am I?
hint: Kolkata's botanical garden has a giant one.

riddle: I am a grass, not a tree, yet I can grow taller than a house, and some of my kind shoot up almost a metre in a single day. Pandas love me. What am I?
hint: Used for scaffolding across Asia.

riddle: Despite my name, I'm a legume, not a true nut. My pods ripen under the soil, and I turn into chikki and a sticky spread. What am I?
hint: Roasted in paper cones on winter evenings.

riddle: Crack open my leathery red skin and you'll find hundreds of juicy red jewels, each one hiding a seed. What am I?
hint: Tough to peel, worth the effort.

riddle: I'm a Mexican salamander who never really grows up: I keep my feathery gills for life, and I can regrow a lost leg and even parts of my heart. What am I?
hint: I always look like I'm smiling.

riddle: I'm the only mammal covered in overlapping scales made of the same stuff as your nails. I have no teeth, I lick up ants with a very long tongue, and I roll into a ball when scared. What am I?
hint: Sadly one of the most trafficked mammals.

riddle: I spend a year or more growing up underwater, but as a winged adult I often live for only a day. I can't even eat as an adult; I just find a mate and die. What am I?
hint: My life as a flyer is shorter than a cricket Test match.

riddle: I'm a finger-length dead-end tube attached to your large intestine. You can live perfectly well without me, but if I swell up, a surgeon has to rush in. What am I?
hint: Its removal ends in -ectomy.

riddle: I spread from person to person with no germs involved. Even reading about me might make your mouth stretch wide open. What am I?
hint: Boring meetings are full of me.

riddle: I have no body, yet I bend trees, fill sails and spin giant blades on hilltops. You feel me on your face but never see me. What am I?
hint: Kites need me.

riddle: Plants perform me using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide, and the leftover gas I release is what you breathe. What process am I?
hint: Green leaves' kitchen.

riddle: I have no colour, smell or taste, and I make up about a fifth of the air. Trees release me for free, fire can't burn without me, and you'd last only minutes without me. What am I?
hint: Hospitals keep cylinders of me.

riddle: I am pure carbon, just like the graphite in your pencil, but my atoms are locked so tightly that I'm the hardest natural material. What am I?
hint: Kohinoor is one of me.

riddle: I am frozen fresh water floating in the salty sea. Only about a tenth of me shows above the surface, so sailors fear the part they can't see. What am I?
hint: The tip is only a small part of the story.

riddle: Twice a day the sea creeps up the beach and slides away again, pulled mostly by the Moon. What are we called?
hint: High and low.

riddle: I am a hole you can look into, but not a hole in the ground. I'm black, and I open wide in the dark and shrink in bright light. What am I?
hint: I also sit in a classroom.

riddle: Twenty of us grow on you all your life, made of the same stuff as a rhino's horn. You trim us often and it never hurts, and most of us show a pale half-moon near the base. What are we?
hint: Nervous people bite us.

riddle: I hatch in a river, spend years growing in the ocean, then swim back upstream, leaping up waterfalls, to the very stream where I was born. What fish am I?
hint: Bears wait at the waterfalls for me.

riddle: My eye is bigger than my brain, and I walk on just two toes per foot. I have wings, but I'd rather outrun a car or kick a lion than fly. What am I?
hint: I don't really bury my head in the sand.

riddle: I begin as an irritating speck trapped inside a shellfish, which coats me in layer after layer until I become a shiny gem. What am I?
hint: Hyderabad is famous for me.

riddle: I'm a fine yellow dust that bees carry from flower to flower, and every spring I make lots of people sneeze. What am I?
hint: Allergy season's culprit.

riddle: I can lie asleep for years inside my tough coat. Give me soil, water and warmth, and I'll wake up, split open and send a root down. What am I?
hint: Every tree started as one of me.

riddle: I'm the reason leaves are green. I trap sunlight so a plant can make food, and in autumn I break down so the reds and yellows can show. What am I?
hint: My name comes from Greek words for 'pale green' and 'leaf'.

riddle: I look like a knobbly root, but I'm really an underground stem. Grated into masala chai, I add a warm, spicy bite. What am I?
hint: Also great for a sore throat.

riddle: I'm the hottest planet, even though I'm not the closest to the Sun, and I spin so slowly that one turn on my axis takes longer than my whole trip around the Sun. What am I?
hint: Earth's so-called twin.

riddle: I'm so dense that not even light can escape my pull. I'm often what remains after a giant star collapses. What am I?
hint: The first photo of one came out in 2019.

riddle: I race through tens of thousands of kilometres of tubes inside you, I get my red colour from iron, and giving away a little of me can save a life. What am I?
hint: Types A, B, AB and O.

riddle: Walk towards me all day and I'll stay just as far away. Ships seem to sink behind me, and the Sun climbs out of me every morning. What am I?
hint: The sun sets below me.

riddle: I'm the only common substance found naturally on Earth as a solid, a liquid and a gas. Oddly, my solid form floats on my liquid form, and no life we know can exist without me. What am I?
hint: Clouds, rivers and glaciers are all made of me.
